_meta.purpose: Goat regions. USDA FSIS: retail cuts of goat are similar to those for lamb or mutton; goat is very lean and a carcass rarely has much fat to protect it from drying; less tender cuts should be braised or stewed; kid lends itself to all lamb recipes. The lamb region scheme is therefore reused with goat-specific notes. No goat-specific industry cut chart was located.
_meta.scores_basis: Editorial, shifted one point leaner than lamb on richness because FSIS describes goat as generally quite lean.

regions.name: Shoulder
regions.short_description: The most flavourful goat cut and the best candidate for low and slow. Lean, so it wants a wrap and a gentle pit.
regions.long_description: FSIS: less tender goat cuts should be braised or stewed, and adult goat is almost always stewed because of its relative toughness, in which form it is flavourful and tender. A smoked goat shoulder is the barbecue version of that advice: smoke for colour, then wrap or braise until it pulls.

retail_cuts.name: Goat shoulder (bone-in)
retail_cuts.note: Wrap earlier than you would a lamb shoulder; there is less fat to lose.

retail_cuts.name: Goat stew meat / curry cut
retail_cuts.note: Bone-in cubes for stews and curries; FSIS: braise or stew.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Roughly 1.5 hours per pound at 225 to 250 F, wrapped for the second half. Approximate.
common_mistakes: Running the pit hot; FSIS: goat dries easily.

regions.name: Rack
regions.short_description: Small, tender, quick. Kid rack cooks like lamb rack (FSIS).
regions.long_description: FSIS: kid meat lends itself to all recipes for lamb, including rack. Smaller than a lamb rack, so it cooks faster and overcooks faster.

retail_cuts.name: Goat rack
retail_cuts.note: Pull 10 F under the target for carryover (Lamb Board method).

retail_cuts.name: Goat rib chops
retail_cuts.note: Very fast; a thermometer through the side.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Shorter than lamb; check early. Approximate.

regions.name: Loin
regions.short_description: Lean and tender. Loin chops for the grill.
regions.long_description: As lamb loin. Very lean; the 145 F final with its rest is the target, not a floor to push past.

regions.name: Leg
regions.short_description: Lean, rich in flavour. Roast it, or smoke it low and slice; braise it if it is from an older animal.
regions.long_description: FSIS: kid leg cooks like lamb leg; adult goat is generally stewed. Age matters more with goat than with any other animal in this spine, and the label rarely says. If it is tough at medium, it wanted the braise.

retail_cuts.name: Goat leg (bone-in)
retail_cuts.note: Kid: roast to 145 F final with rest. Adult: braise.

regions.planning_time_guidance: As lamb leg for kid; longer, moist, for adult. Approximate.
common_mistakes: Treating an older animal's leg as a roast.

regions.name: Breast
regions.short_description: Ribs and breast. The most connective tissue and the most of what little fat goat has. Stew, braise, or smoke low with a wrap.
regions.long_description: As lamb breast, leaner. Goat ribs take a dry rub well but need moisture to soften.

retail_cuts.name: Goat ribs
retail_cuts.note: Wrap with a splash of liquid after the smoke sets.

retail_cuts.name: Goat breast
retail_cuts.note: FSIS: braise or stew less tender cuts.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 3 to 4 hours at 250 F, wrapped for the second half. Approximate.
common_mistakes: Dry, unwrapped cook to the end.

regions.name: Flank
regions.short_description: Thin and lean. Marinate, grill hot, slice thin, or grind.
regions.long_description: As lamb flank. On a small goat carcass this is a modest strip, often ground.

regions.name: Shank
regions.short_description: Tough and delicious after a long braise. Osso buco, birria, curry.
regions.long_description: As lamb shank. FSIS: braise or stew. The smoke-then-braise method gives a goat shank smoke flavour without drying it.

retail_cuts.name: Goat shank
retail_cuts.note: Fall-off-the-bone is the target, well past any doneness scale.
